summary: Retired steel tower on Wray's Hill, last used 1988; a Huntingdon Daily News column says it still stands. A wooden tower came before it.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with a glass-enclosed cab; earlier tower was wooden
facts.status_note: Retired after its last use on March 28, 1988; a Huntingdon Daily News column says it still stands.
facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Forests and Waters (district office disputed: Huntingdon per the 1972 account, Rothrock per the column)

events.note: A 1926 newspaper item gives 1920 for a 55-foot wooden tower near Robertsdale. The Echoes column dates a wooden tower to 1924-25, and the 1972 account to 1927.
The 1972 account says the present steel tower was constructed in 1942 on land belonging to the Rockhill Coal Company. The 1941 survey description already describes a steel tower.
Photo caption places Ike Williams at the top watching for fires during the early 1960s. Year is a decade marker only.
Column says the tower was last used on March 28, 1988, and that the last person to work in it is believed to have been Ann D. Wilson of Todd.

corrections.why: Both the 1972 account and the Echoes column give 2,336 feet above sea level, which is about 712 m. The record's 706 m is about 2,316 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Dates for the first wooden tower differ: 1920 (1926 item, near Robertsdale), 1924-25 (column, northwest of Wood), 1927 (1972 account, northwest of Woodvale). Story reports all three and does not pick one.
The 1941 survey description already shows a steel tower, while the 1972 account gives 1942 for construction. Record keeps 1942 as the replacement year with the 1941 description noted.
The 1941 survey says about 65 feet (19.8 m); the 1972 account and the column say 60 feet (18.3 m). Facts use 18.3 m, the figure in the later accounts.
The 1972 account says the Huntingdon District office maintained the tower. The column says the Rothrock District forest office controlled it. Story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Column text is from the cached article. A second Echoes URL (columnist-details-history-of-retired-rockhill-fire-tower) returned HTTP 429 and was not read; a search snippet from it matches the same facts. The column is undated in the cache. No source found on public access or on the hilltop today beyond 'still rises'. The column calls the first wooden tower the Round Mountain Tower, which may be a separate tower; the Weebly page calls it Rockhill. A firetower.org guess URL returned 404. Record agency reads 'Rothrock State Forest' and the 1941 survey says PA Dept of Forests and Waters; the Echoes column says Rothrock District forest office.
